What the next step is
§16.3 scenario 10 — Counter_ClosesSitting_TableFlipsToSettledAndTotalsMatch. I traced every surface it touches and the design is settled:

Arrangement: administrator + soup (6.50) + pie (14.00) + table + a real counter account (§3.7 → §3.5 forced password change, reusing Slice 12's CreateStaffAccountAsync / SignInWithPasswordAsync / CompleteForcedPasswordChangeAsync). The counter account is warranted here for the opposite reason to scenario 9's: §6.5.8 admits an administrator's corrective events after a close, so asserting "read-only" as an administrator asserts the wrong side of the claim.
Guest sends soup ×1 + pie ×2; the administrator's kitchen board fulfills the soup only, so the bill is mixed and §5.3's pending-line warning has exactly one line to name.
Seven independent computations of the same number get asserted equal: the till header (SQL sitting_bill), the confirm prompt's CurrentTotalAmount, the post-close stamped header, .counter-settle-total (C# sum), the guest's "Table total" and "Your total" on the other circuit, and the settled_total_amount column.

M6 Slice 13 — §16.3 scenario 10. Eight full files, extracting at the repo root:

bash
tar -xzf m6-slice13-close-and-settle.tar.gz -C /home/kushal/src/dotnet/myrestaurant
Files to DELETE: none. No migration, no schema change, no package change, no ADR edit, no Program.cs edit, no .slnx edit.

On "some tests are now failing"
They aren't. claude-terminal.txt is from the same commit as dump.txt (b6a2892) and is green throughout — 971/0 failed, all six ci_local.sh gates, and E2E at 15/0 failed/12 passed/3 skipped. The 15 skips under a plain dotnet test are the E2E scenarios opting out with MYRESTAURANT_E2E unset; the 3 are the unimplemented §16.3 scenarios. This takes one, leaving two.

What's in it
Scenario 10 asserts one total through seven independent computations — the till header (SQL sum), the confirmation prompt (CurrentTotalAmount quoted directly), the post-close header (the stamped value), the settle panel (C# sum), both guest totals on another circuit, and table_sitting.settled_total_amount itself. Six of those are render-time reads of the same view and could all agree on a close that stamped nothing; only the column carries §5.3's actual promise.

The bill is deliberately mixed — one soup delivered, two pies that never leave the kitchen — because the pending-line warning must name one line, not two portions, and because at one of each item a total that summed unit prices instead of extensions would be indistinguishable from the correct one.

Two additive product changes, both with the tag tree verified identical: #counter-close / #counter-close-confirm (the two-step confirm was otherwise the same selector twice, and settling can't be undone), and .order-settled-heading (every other marker of §11.1's flip is an absence, which a dead circuit also produces).

One thing worth flagging
My dump splitter reconstructed nine files imperfectly — export.sh contains a literal # FILE: line that broke its boundary detection, and a few others lose trailing #-only or blank lines. None of them are in this archive. I verified all seven pre-existing files against the SHA-256 hashes export.sh recorded before editing anything, and all seven matched, so every byte I didn't touch is known to match your tree. I also diffed each shipped file against a pristine reconstruction and inspected all twelve removed lines individually — every one is a line I reopened with an added attribute, plus the scenario 10 placeholder.

Expected after this: dotnet test unchanged at 971/0/956/15, and MYRESTAURANT_E2E=1 at 15 total / 0 failed / 13 passed / 2 skipped. Scenario 10 adds roughly 25–30s and waits on no timer.

Next is scenario 11 — hide, filter, unhide — whose arrangement is this scenario's ending, since a hideable order is a settled one.
